clue.text: Punctured tyre fixed by cast-iron bicycle pump?

indicators.note: the punctured tyre is held fast by the cast letters around it, so it sits inside them
cast-iron read as iron that has been cast, i.e. its letters thrown into a new shape

parts.note: a punctured tyre is a flat

explanation.surface: A cyclist with a puncture uses a sturdy cast-iron pump to fix the tyre.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'cast-iron' hides the split: 'cast' is the anagram signal, giving INOR, and 'fixed by' is the container. The question mark flags a pump as a fanciful example.
explanation.definitionFit: A bicycle pump is one kind of device that pumps air in, so it is an example of an inflator.

clue.text: Effect of setter's agreement

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself: setter's = setter is = I'M
a pact is an agreement

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter wonders what effect his agreement will have.
explanation.definitionFit: Impact as a noun is the effect or influence something has, a straight synonym.

clue.text: It's fine — fine to threaten your leader

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
to lour is to look threatening, as a dark sky does

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of your

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a fine imposed for threatening their boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Floury describes something powdery and fine-grained like flour, so it is a sense of fine.

clue.text: Skinny, topless, stops a skinny woman giving advice

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so this piece fills the middle of the other

parts.note: gaunt means skinny

indicators.note: topless means the top letter of the word is removed

parts.note: bony means skinny

explanation.surface: Skinny, the setter, stripped off and interrupted a thin woman handing out advice.
explanation.walkthrough: Skinny is this puzzle's setter, which tempts a self-reference, but here it just means bony. 'topless' leaves ONY, which 'stops' places in A GAUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: An agony aunt writes the problem-page column in a magazine, offering readers advice on their personal troubles.

clue.text: Spent lesson getting confused with logs? Neat!

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled up, so the three words are mixed together

explanation.surface: A spent lesson muddled up with logbooks, and someone cheers sarcastically.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on their last legs is exhausted or nearly finished, the idiomatic sense of spent.

clue.text: Part of apprenticeship has education in stages

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An apprenticeship includes education delivered gradually, step by step.
explanation.definitionFit: Something phased is introduced gradually, one step after another, rather than all at once.

clue.text: Suffering over? That's welcome

parts.note: hell is great suffering
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Someone relieved that their suffering is finished calls it welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Hello is a word of greeting, the welcome given to someone arriving.

clue.text: Explained about United's closure

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: shown can mean explained or demonstrated
Utd is the usual abbreviation for United in football team names

explanation.surface: A report explains why a football club, United, is closing down.
explanation.definitionFit: A shutdown is the closing of a business or system, so it means a closure.

clue.text: Last of intrepid explorers vacated ancient city's ruins

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, here of intrepid
a vacated word has had its insides emptied out, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: Troy is the ancient city, and the 's makes it Troy's

explanation.surface: Bold explorers abandon the ruins of an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruins' looks like a noun in the surface but is the verb: one who ruins something destroys it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruin something is to wreck or demolish it, a synonym of destroying.

clue.text: A macabre giggle disturbed part of airport

indicators.note: disturbed letters are thrown out of their order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sinister giggle unsettles people.
explanation.definitionFit: Baggage reclaim is the hall at an airport terminal where arriving passengers collect their luggage.

clue.text: Bulk of research by Lennon's partner is voluntary

indicators.note: the bulk of a word is most of it, all bar the last letter

parts.note: to probe is to research or investigate
Yoko Ono was the wife and partner of John Lennon

explanation.surface: Most research done alongside Yoko Ono is unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro bono work, from the Latin for the public good, is professional work done without a fee.

clue.text: Every cake's icing, according to Spooner, is done with gusto

parts.note: all can mean every

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, so the first sounds are exchanged

parts.note: buns are small cakes; every cake's = all buns'
glazing is a sugary icing coat on a bun

explanation.surface: The icing on every cake gets spread with enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Going in all guns blazing means acting with full force and energy, an idiom for great gusto.

clue.text: Seek to ingratiate oneself with character of 14 that's out of line

indicators.note: out of means the following letter is taken away, leaving the rest

parts.note: mulligatawny (14 across) is a spiced soup, so its character is the taste of its spice, its flavour

explanation.surface: A soup's spicy flavour is described as something oddly out of line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of line' looks like misbehaviour, but it means L removed from FLAVOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To curry favour is to try to win someone's approval through flattery, an idiom for ingratiating.

clue.text: Urge control about introduction of dry culinary ingredient

parts.note: to egg on is to urge

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: power means control

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter, here of dry

explanation.surface: A cook is urged to control how much dry ingredient goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg powder is dried egg, an ingredient used in baking and cooking.

clue.text: I'll put back into cup a golden soup

indicators.note: into means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a mug is a kind of cup

indicators.note: put back means the word is reversed, written back to front

parts.note: I'll gives its letters as written, without the apostrophe
tawny is a golden-brown colour

explanation.surface: Someone puts a golden drink back into a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Mulligatawny is a spicy curried soup that originated in Anglo-Indian cooking.

clue.text: Still standing naked, so it's said, carrying extremely dilapidated toy

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other
standing in a down clue means the word is set upright, read from bottom to top

parts.note: yet means still

indicators.note: extremely means the extreme letters, first and last
so it's said means a word that sounds like another is wanted

parts.note: bare means naked

explanation.surface: An old, battered, bald plush toy is still upright.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'standing' reads upward, giving TEY; 'carrying' and 'extremely' then work inside it, and 'so it's said' is the sound-alike signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A teddy bear is a soft stuffed toy bear, a classic children's toy.

clue.text: Shaking with fear, a soprano tackles a bit of Mozart

indicators.note: to tackle something is to take hold of it, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a treble is a boy soprano

indicators.note: a bit of a word is just its first letter, here of Mozart

explanation.surface: A soprano singer attempts some Mozart and trembles with nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: Atremble is a literary adjective for trembling, typically from fright or nerves.

clue.text: Distraught baker has endless oven trouble, finally cracking

indicators.note: distraught means upset and disordered, so the letters are rearranged
endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: an Aga is a British range-style cooker, an oven

indicators.note: finally means the last letter, here of trouble

explanation.surface: A baker is upset because the oven is giving endless trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracking' looks like a modifier at the end, but it is the definition, a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakage is the act of something breaking or cracking, so it matches the noun cracking.

clue.text: Conflicted by rubbish wines being savagely criticised

parts.note: torn means conflicted or undecided
tosh is rubbish, nonsense
reds are red wines

explanation.surface: A critic is in two minds about cheap wines being savaged.
explanation.definitionFit: Tearing something to shreds means attacking it fiercely in criticism, an idiomatic usage.

clue.text: It's attractive to imagine The Devil in conversation

indicators.note: in conversation means said out loud, so a word sounding alike is wanted

parts.note: to see something in the mind is to imagine it; Old Nick is a traditional nickname for the Devil

explanation.surface: Someone claims picturing the Devil is pleasing to talk about.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Nick is a traditional English nickname for the Devil.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenic place has pleasing natural views, so it is attractive to look at.

clue.text: See 12
Missionary given lace pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are rubbishly rearranged

explanation.surface: A missionary is given lace underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' reads as underwear but is the anagram signal, from its British slang sense of bad or rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangelic describes spreading the Christian gospel, as missionaries do, so it is an adjective for missionary.

clue.text: One inspired by award is making progress

indicators.note: inspired literally means breathed in, so one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal or award
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone motivated by winning a prize is getting ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Going can mean moving forward or advancing, as in 'it's going well'.

clue.text: Odd bits of your cocoa plant

indicators.note: odd bits are the letters in odd positions, first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: A few scraps of your cocoa plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The yucca is a spiky-leaved plant of the agave family from the Americas.

clue.text: See 11
Corroded a metal until tip of electrode's absorbed

indicators.note: absorbed means taken in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: tin is a metal

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter, here of electrode

parts.note: to can mean until, as in 'nine to five'

explanation.surface: A metal is corroded until an electrode is soaked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid that eats into metal wears it away chemically, which is what corroding means.

clue.text: Come out — for example with army corps retreating

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: An army unit, for instance, is pulling back.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to appear or come into view, the same as coming out.

clue.text: Large amount of data seized by career criminal — he may nobble the jury

indicators.note: seized by means held within, so one piece goes inside the other
criminal means wrong or bent, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: MB is a megabyte, a large amount of computer data

explanation.surface: A career criminal grabs a hoard of data.
explanation.walkthrough: Embracery is the legal offence of trying to corrupt or bribe a jury, and an embracer commits it.
explanation.definitionFit: To nobble is to tamper with by bribery or threat, which is exactly what this legal term describes.
